fiveW.who: Northern states (Union, Lincoln) vs Southern states (Confederacy, Jefferson Davis)
fiveW.what: Civil War — the 'War Between the States'
fiveW.why: Slavery; conflicting economic interests and cultures; secession of the South
fiveW.how: Southern states seceded; Lincoln fought to restore the Union; the North won

notes.content:
**Executive summary:** The **American Civil War (1861–65)** was fought between the northern and southern states over **slavery**, to uphold **liberty and equality**.

**Background**
• The **Industrial Revolution** in England created huge demand for **raw cotton** → southern plantations grew cotton → needed **cheap labour** → **African slaves**.
• **Cultural divide:** industrial **North** — city life, mixed cultures and classes; agricultural **South** — the **exclusive culture of plantation owners**.
• By the mid-19th century slavery was seen as a **social evil** and **abolished throughout the British Empire**; the North did not need slaves and opposed slavery.

| North | South |
|---|---|
| **Manufacturing and shipping** centres | **Agricultural**, dependent on plantation estates |
| Industrial cities; no need for slaves | Cotton plantations needed **slave labour** |
| Opposed slavery; anti-slavery movements | Defended slavery; treated slaves cruelly |
| Mixed, open city culture | Exclusive plantation culture |

Different economies → different cultures and world views → disagreement on many issues, **especially slavery**.

fiveW.who: Abolitionists of the North; Harriet Beecher Stowe
fiveW.why: Cruel and unjust treatment of slaves
fiveW.how: Protests; the novel Uncle Tom's Cabin changed public opinion

notes.content:
• **Anti-slavery movements** arose in the **19th century**; played a **significant role** in causing the war.
• **Fugitive Slave Act (1850):** let slave owners travel north to **capture escaped slaves** — hugely **unpopular** in the North.
• **Uncle Tom's Cabin (1852)** by **Harriet Beecher Stowe** showed the evils of slavery → changed northern opinion → boosted **abolition**.
• Facing abolition, southern states threatened to **secede** (break away).

**Keyword — Abolitionists:** northerners who fought against slavery and demanded its abolition.

fiveW.who: Abraham Lincoln (16th President); South Carolina + 10 states; Jefferson Davis
fiveW.what: Southern states left the Union and formed the Confederate States of America
fiveW.how: South Carolina seceded first; ten more followed

notes.content:
• **Abraham Lincoln** elected **16th President**; opposed slavery as a violation of 'all men are created equal'.
• **South Carolina** — **first state to break off** from the Union.
• **Ten more seceded:** Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina, Tennessee.
• **1861 — Confederate States of America** formed; President **Jefferson Davis**.

**Memory trick:** 1 + 10 = **11 Confederate states**.

fiveW.who: Union under Lincoln and the Republican Party; Confederate General Robert E. Lee
fiveW.where: Across the USA; ended at Appomattox Court House
fiveW.what: War to bring the southern states back into the Union
fiveW.why: Lincoln would not allow the Union to break up
fiveW.how: Four years of fighting; North gained the upper hand by Sept 1864; Lee surrendered

notes.content:
• War broke out in **April 1861**; Lincoln and the **Republican Party** were determined to keep the Union together.
• **Over 6,00,000 soldiers killed**.
• By **September 1864** the North had the upper hand.
• **April 1865 — General Robert E. Lee surrendered at Appomattox Court House** → end of the war.
• **Robert E. Lee** commanded the **Confederate Army of Northern Virginia**.

**Republican Party:** founded by anti-slavery activists in **1854**.

• **Proclamation of Emancipation:** Lincoln declared all southern states **free of slavery** → title **'Great Emancipator'**.
• He planned a **liberal reconstruction** of the South, but was **assassinated in 1865** (first US President to be assassinated).
• **Military rule** was imposed on the South; **reconstruction ended in 1876**.

**Result:** Union preserved; slavery abolished; African-Americans freed from bondage.

notes.subtopic: 7. Abraham Lincoln and the Gettysburg Address

fiveW.why: To honour the fallen and rededicate the nation to freedom and equality
fiveW.how: 'Government of the people, by the people, for the people'

notes.content:
**Lincoln's life**
• Born **1809, Kentucky**; worked as a **clerk**, then joined the military.
• **1860** — won **40%** of the popular vote.
• **Achievements:** held the **Union together**, led the North to **victory**, **emancipated** African-Americans; a great **orator**.

**Gettysburg Address — 19 Nov 1863, Pennsylvania**
• 'Four score and seven years ago…' — a nation **conceived in Liberty**, dedicated to the idea that **all men are created equal** (implicitly against slavery).
• Called for a **'new birth of freedom'**.
• Defined democracy: **'government of the people, by the people, for the people'**.

questions.question: 'The anti-slavery movements played a significant role in the outbreak of the Civil War.' Do you agree? Give reasons.
questions.answer:
Yes.

  • Abolitionists in the North demanded the end of slavery, deepening the North–South divide.
  • The Fugitive Slave Act (1850) angered the North.
  • Uncle Tom's Cabin (1852) turned public opinion against slavery.
  • Fearing abolition — especially after anti-slavery Lincoln's election — the South seceded, which led to war.
questions.topperTip: Build a chain: movement → Act → book → Lincoln → secession → war.

questions.question: What impact did the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850 have on the northern states?
questions.answer: It allowed slave owners to travel to the North and capture escaped slaves. It was hugely unpopular with the anti-slavery forces in the North and increased sympathy for the abolitionists.

questions.question: How is Uncle Tom's Cabin significant to the history of the Civil War?
questions.answer: Written by Harriet Beecher Stowe (1852), it exposed the evils of slavery, changed how northerners viewed slavery, furthered the cause of abolition and contributed to the outbreak of the Civil War.

questions.question: Name five states that seceded from the Union. When was the Confederacy formed?
questions.answer: South Carolina, Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia (also Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina, Tennessee). The Confederate States of America was formed in 1861 with Jefferson Davis as President.

questions.question: Describe the course and end of the American Civil War.
questions.answer:
• Began in April 1861 — Lincoln and the Republicans refused to let the Union break up.
  • Over 6,00,000 soldiers killed.
  • North gained the upper hand by September 1864.
  • Ended in April 1865 with General Lee's surrender at Appomattox Court House.
  • Lincoln's Proclamation of Emancipation freed slaves in the South.

questions.question: Mention the accomplishments of Abraham Lincoln as President.
questions.answer:
• Held the Union together.
  • Led the North to victory in the Civil War.
  • Abolished slavery in the South (Proclamation of Emancipation) — 'Great Emancipator'.
  • A great orator — the Gettysburg Address defined democracy.

questions.question: (Source) From the Gettysburg Address: what does Lincoln say about slavery, and how does he describe democracy?
questions.answer:
• Slavery: the nation was 'dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal' — so slavery goes against its founding idea; he calls for a 'new birth of freedom'.
  • Democracy: 'government of the people, by the people, for the people'.
  • Importance: it explains the moral purpose of the war — freedom and equality.
keywords: of the people, by the people, for the people
questions.topperTip: Quote the exact line on democracy — it's the most-asked line of the chapter.

questions.question: (Picture) Name the 16th President. When did he become President? Why was he assassinated?
questions.answer:
• (a) Abraham Lincoln.
  • (b) Elected in 1860 (took office 1861).
  • (c) Assassinated in 1865 by a Confederate sympathiser who opposed his anti-slavery policies and the Union victory.
